basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 64.' and it opens 'Vers. 64. Rebecca conspecto Isaac de camelo descendit. Quia Ecclesia cognito Christo se'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 64. Rebecca conspecto Isaac de camelo descendit. Quia Ecclesia cognito Christo se pro suis erroribus confusa humiliavit. Unde et bene se pallio operuisse dicitur, quia confusione et erroris sui rubore se operuit. Unde et Paulus quibusdam loquitur: Quem fructum habuistis tunc in his, in quibus nunc erubescitis? (Rom. VI, 21.) Nam et Psalmista dicit: Operuit confusio faciem meam (Psal. LXVIII, 8).
